conditions: Fixed mass, no phase change, specified heating process with relevant specific heat capacity approximately constant over the temperature interval; use the appropriate process heat capacity. Q is net heat into the sample; the product is exact for constant process heat capacity.
spoken_aliases: q equals m times c times delta t
heat transferred equals mass times specific heat capacity times the change in temperature

evidence: For a specified heating process, the heat capacity per unit mass is the heat increment per mass per temperature increment. Integrate m c dT with fixed m and constant c to get m c times the temperature change. If c varies, the integral rather than the product is required.
Reference checked 2026-11-27: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-2/pages/1-key-equations. Proposed maintainer approval, not independent human certification.
